64169c8c9e3e95678dcd0fe8ef71a1bbd5298056.summary: Socket reports 13 malicious NuGet packages used in a campaign that lures .NET developers with fake take-home job assessments. Building or running a lure project triggers a build-time MSBuild stager and a runtime control that launches a DLL side-loading pair. Other packages download and run executables from GitHub. Related fake axios repositories carry loaders and a Chrome profile stealer, and a trojanized crypto wallet app was also used. The campaign is not attributed to a named threat actor.

hedges: We could not determine how the Home Assessment lures reach candidates; we found no recruiter message, email or job post for them.
We have not attributed this campaign to a named threat actor.
Take-home tests resemble lures that public reporting links to North Korea, but no shared indicator or code was found with published campaigns.
We did not test the side-load, and whether a copied osk.exe starts from the user's local app data folder on current Windows builds remains an open question.
Download counts include mirrors and scanners and are not victim counts.
We could not determine whether the repository belongs to the threat actor or to a targeted developer, so we do not name it.
The link between WinUI.Button and the rest of the cluster rests on naming and technique, not a shared indicator.
We treat that as timing evidence only.

64ad1c2eda90282e964bf03c1d2879c8525be61c.summary: This page is a rule entry in the YARAhub repository of YARA detection rules, not a threat report. The entry is named mal_jinxv2loader, with the description 'JinxLoader V2 Payload', date added 2023-10-03, rule matching TLP:WHITE and rule sharing TLP:RED. It lists a reference MD5 hash and an archive date of 2026-11-25. It gives no analysis of actors, campaigns, techniques or victims, so no facts are recorded.

6431c1c21d4cce6686b3b44d057f31b66e817aba.summary: The report covers the disclosure by Aflac, a US supplemental insurer, of a breach in a wider campaign against US insurance companies. An Aflac spokesperson could not attribute the breach to a group, but the report says it shows all the signs of Scattered Spider. Aflac said its systems were not affected by ransomware and the intrusion was stopped within hours. Personal and health information may have been stolen. The report describes Scattered Spider as a social engineering actor that used MFA bombing and SIM swapping, breached MGM Resorts in September 2023, and partnered with other…

64827e1bc8da8e53ee871703e5844d4e7e36a504.summary: ENISA's Threat Landscape Report 2018 (ETL 2018, published January 2019) reviews the top 15 cyberthreats for December 2017 to December 2018, drawing on open-source material, MISP, CERT-EU and a commercial intelligence portal. It covers malware (fileless attacks, cryptojacking, the VPNFilter router campaign, Triton), web-based and web application attacks, phishing and business email compromise, ransomware, data breaches and cyber espionage. It gives trends, statistics and mitigation advice, plus threat agent profiles, attack vector notes and policy and research conclusions on cyber threat…
